_anchors.canvas.w: 64, the subject's cell. Roll is about screen x, so the machine's LENGTH is invariant through the whole turn and the width needs no roll margin at all.
_anchors.canvas.h: 48, and THIS clip is why: at the quarter turn the 30 px top-wing span stands vertical, 15 px either side of the hull axis. The cell is sized by this clip's worst frame and shared by the other two.
_anchors.canvas.originY: 26 — the hull axis, which is the centre of the barrel roll. An off-centre origin would swing the machine out of its cell mid-turn: the skate's originY anchor, transferred.
_anchors.frames.walk: 13, the kickflip's arithmetic re-derived for a wing: (n-1) divisible by four for the five phases, and 30° between frames. The top wing is 1.2 px thick and 26 px deep — at 45° steps it would jump from edge to more than half its full face between two frames; at 30° each quarter turn shows three readable widths.
_anchors.light.x: -0.5, shared with the subject's other clips.
_anchors.light.z: -0.3, shared — and load-bearing here: both wing FACES must be legible as the roll trades them, which is what this front component buys.
_anchors.gait.swing: 0.14 turn. The roll clip's largest angle key is 0.1 on the hull — 5° of climbing attitude under the turn. The rotation of this clip is NOT on this channel, which is the whole point of gait.roll existing.
_anchors.gait.lift: 2.4 px, the climb's value: the runtime carries the arc.
_anchors.gait.roll: 1 turn — this file exists for this number, as skate-flip.json existed for its. At amplitude 1 a roll key IS a fraction of a revolution, so the hull's track runs 0 to -1 and means one whole barrel roll. THE TRANSFER: the same knob that turned a 10-part plank now turns a 21-part machine about its root.
_anchors.texture.dither: 0, the body rule from the skate round, carried with its measurement.
_anchors.shadow.steps: 7, as the cruise: one sun on one subject.
_anchors.fill.x: 0.45, opposite the key, as the cruise.
_anchors.fill.y: 0.4, from below — and through the inverted half of the roll this IS the light that keeps the crimson top faces readable while they hang toward the ground.
_anchors.fill.z: -0.3, matching the key, as the cruise.
_anchors.fill.weight: 0.1, the street's value, as the cruise.
_anchors.playback.msPerFrame: 40: thirteen frames make a 520 ms roll. The second impulse buys roughly 0.75 s of air from where it is pressed, so the turn completes with margin and the hold on the last frame is a level plane, never a frozen half-roll.
